newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends lower in bearish sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends lower in bearish sentiment.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed on Friday at a low approaching those last seen in January 1995, after prices were pushed down in two-way trade below London's Thursday finish, gold dealers said.
Morning trade kicked off with sales from Japanese traders on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) in the wake of more dollar/yen swings, dealers said.
"In the afternoon they simply shortcovered their positions," said one trader.
But afternoon trade saw more selling pressure from Europe as bearish sentiment continued to cloud the market, and gold was seen heading towards US$370 per ounce, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$371.60/372.10 an ounce Friday against London's US$372.45/95 close on Thursday.
Local gold ended HK$4 lower at HK$3,433 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -6.00 from its previous fix at +5.00.
Tael gold was trading at a premium to spot gold, at the equivalent of US$372.20/70 per ounce, dealers noted.
"Good demand for physical gold has pushed up prices of tael gold," said a bullion trader at a European bank, noting the gap between the tael and spot markets had created arbirtrage opportunities.
